lxc_c4f728c8aac7b5b4.text: Spanish people and everyday life, a little history, regions and languages, famous places, food and meals, and the Seville Fair with flamenco all help explain Spain.

lxc_787815832a804f4e.text: Spain is in southern and western Europe.

lxc_48e33cedea779005.text: It covers most of the Iberian Peninsula, the land it shares with Portugal.

lxc_715379ccf65b850e.text: France and Andorra are to the north.

lxc_bd7f8fc00ac62e42.text: Madrid is Spain’s capital and largest city.

lxc_a2985293b42756a0.text: Other big cities include Barcelona, Valencia, Seville, and Bilbao.

lxc_3fd1241a1adce498.text: Spain also includes islands: the Canary Islands in the Atlantic Ocean and the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean Sea.

lxc_dc7172ad964a9cec.text: So everyday life has many different settings, from a large city to an island.

lxc_ad61279ef4a403c9.text: Meal times give us another way to understand daily life.

lxc_dcd43fac3e8c501e.text: Dinner in Spain often starts from about 8:30 in the evening.

lxc_9260ac8dddc6fce8.text: From 711 to 1492, Muslim-ruled lands on the Iberian Peninsula were called Al-Andalus.

lxc_6db34eabbc61840e.text: The Alhambra, a palace and fortress in Granada, connects us with that time.

lxc_15f0d38434553986.text: A fortress is a strong building made to protect a place.

lxc_76ca176145dbfcf3.text: In 1492, Granada’s Muslim kingdom surrendered to Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand, known as the Catholic Monarchs.

lxc_dcf05cd712f2b54c.text: That same year, Christopher Columbus sailed to the Americas on a journey paid for by Isabella.

lxc_cd19b984dbe73162.text: Much later, the Spanish Civil War lasted from 1936 to 1939.

lxc_4084d34278d324ad.text: This sets out the country’s main rules.

lxc_2cf68572f62ee3fc.text: Today, Spain is a democracy with a king, and it belongs to the European Union.

lxc_11d461f75677ab2f.text: An autonomous community is a region with its own government.

lxc_8973e317866423f6.text: Andalusia is in the south, Catalonia is in the north-east, and Galicia is in the north-west.

lxc_04facc375d40d030.text: The Basque Country is in the north.

lxc_da0e95344b6631dd.text: Spanish, also called Castilian, is the official national language.

lxc_4f99b912dfbfd7c9.text: But some regions have another official language next to Spanish.

lxc_0daa99f7a1d1de52.text: Catalan is spoken around Barcelona in Catalonia.

lxc_73018d041cf150bb.text: It is called Valencian in Valencia.

lxc_ce468dfc325f0642.text: Galician is spoken in Galicia, and Basque is spoken in the Basque Country, including Bilbao.

lxc_a5926418de55758b.text: Basque is not related to Spanish or to most other European languages.

lxc_9e9b8412e6a7f70b.text: These differences are part of Spain’s local life.

lxc_81bafbe4fc68129a.text: Let’s connect three cities with three famous places.

lxc_a908d34b0e580963.text: In Barcelona, the Sagrada Familia is a Catholic church designed by Antoni Gaudi.

lxc_0fdf8a3c912ddcf5.text: It is the tallest church in the world, and parts of it are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

lxc_5e39c126357e853a.text: In Granada, Andalusia, the Alhambra brings us back to Al-Andalus.

lxc_ecef70bc4532b0d8.text: This old palace and fortress is a famous example of Islamic building design.

lxc_cf86a720fbc12398.text: In central Madrid, the Museo del Prado is Spain’s main national art museum.

lxc_1ffe59f7d9d08b0a.text: It opened in 1819 and has many paintings by Francisco Goya and Diego Velazquez.

lxc_eeec72ae2b39421e.text: These places offer different ways to explore Spain: through a church, a palace, or art.

lxc_63658a2d80bf7fcf.text: Lunch is usually Spain’s large main meal, starting around 2:00 to 2:30 in the afternoon.

lxc_db728e5a10bf2f8c.text: A small snack, called merienda, may come around 6:00.

lxc_56f48cb3bfb35dc3.text: After a meal, people may stay at the table to relax and talk.

lxc_0f6bab6ac2d03574.text: This time together is called sobremesa.

lxc_0de0419d66806a03.text: Paella is a Valencian rice dish from the east coast, cooked in a wide, flat pan.

lxc_7cf761619bc70acb.text: Gazpacho is an Andalusian cold vegetable soup, often made with tomato and eaten in summer.

lxc_a4e78a16233e0e02.text: Tortilla is a thick omelette with eggs and potatoes, often with onion.

lxc_2d936beac6b5d3cf.text: Tapas are small snacks that can be hot or cold.

lxc_678f7017e3e67e9d.text: Several tapas together can make a full meal.

lxc_5e97394916d4144c.text: The Seville Fair, also called Feria de Abril, is an Andalusian fair in Seville.

lxc_267dbba0d60dcf6f.text: It usually begins two weeks after Holy Week, the week before Easter.

lxc_1bc2725962e48158.text: The fair has rows of decorated tents called casetas.

lxc_fc2cb1011d647405.text: These belong to families, groups of friends, clubs, and other groups.

lxc_e15705533df60222.text: From about nine at night until early morning, people dance sevillanas, a folk dance danced in pairs.

lxc_e8a10d1bbdbbc058.text: Southern Spain is also the home of flamenco.

lxc_4f7f73629a1d7798.text: Flamenco is an Andalusian art of music, song, and dance.

lxc_2a22d52cb4ae47e1.text: The Romani people of Andalusia helped create it.

lxc_1385842735b65777.text: Like Valencian paella, flamenco has a local home, even though people know it far beyond that region.
